test_method.procedure_description: ASTM G5 1-L multineck flask, platinum counter electrode and SCE positioned in a salt bridge with a high-silica tip. Anodic polarization from the corrosion potential in deaerated 4 M NaCl at 80°C; five tests per alloy. Printed representative pitting potentials are described as close to the five-test averages. A pitting-scan rate is not independently stated; the 1-mV/s ramp is explicitly given for the CPT protocol.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Pitting potential from the anodic polarization response. No numerical onset-current threshold is specified.

experiments.result_note: Printed representative pitting potential, described as close to the average of five polarization tests per alloy. The text assigns 609 to 3% Mo and 515 to 2% W–2% Mo, whereas Figure 1’s solid/dotted curve ordering appears reversed. The explicit text assignment is preserved; no onset was independently inferred from the unannotated curves. The general 30–100 mV scatter statement is not an alloy-specific error interval. Composition is Table 1 bulk chemistry (wt% basis stated in the experimental discussion), with Fe explicitly balance. The 3% Mo W dash remains null rather than an inferred zero; phase-specific EDX analyses in Tables 3/4 do not replace bulk composition. TEM-foil preparation and KOH metallographic etching are not assigned to the pitting electrodes.

test_method.procedure_description: ASTM G5 1-L multineck flask, platinum counter electrode and SCE positioned in a salt bridge with a high-silica tip. Polarize from corrosion potential to 600 mV (SCE) at 1 mV/s, then hold at 600 mV while heating the deaerated 4-M NaCl solution at 0.5°C/min from 40°C and monitoring anodic current. CPT measured at least four times per alloy. The test_temperature field is the associated CPT, not a constant bath temperature.
test_method.pitting_criterion: CPT is the solution temperature at which anodic current increases abruptly, indicating pitting. Pitting at the imposed 600 mV gives the registered upper bound on potential; it is not a swept onset potential.
